# October 31st (1): Getting on Track

I am brand new to everything in hardware, Half Life is the first time I've ever done these kinds of things. Because of this, the new starter project guide style confused me, and left me very lost without a structured tutorial to follow. I knew what I wanted to make, just no idea how to start. I added 2 parts in my schematic, ones I remember from previous projects and just stared at them, no idea what do next.

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 2.52.49 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/25b7d795f89ff131f844af197a25d0bbe1fbf66e13f5173cc3aca16bcd92b7ac.png)

Which pin is VCC and which one is GND?  Do I have to add in the glass panel by myself? If I don't, will I not have one? Do I need a glass panel? What's a LiPo? What parts do I need?

Thus, I spent one hour with my father looking through the OLED screen guide and just... orienting myself.

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 3.01.01 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/4abddaa2ec6265820c60753dfd034ead55f0cb733e714629dd7cc08fab643b15.png)

I have to check the listing for the order of the pins to know which is which, and wire them in order. Yes, I need a glass panel, and I can buy them preassembled if adding them in is too complicated. A LiPo is a battery, a rechargeable power source. I need the microcontroller and OLED screen, and also decided on adding 4 buttons to cycle between focus and breaks and reset the timer.

Many such questions were answered. A plan was formed. I was no longer wandering around aimlessly, I had a direction labelled on a roadmap to success.

I don't know for sure if these count toward approved hours... but it was a lot of work. Journalling them anyways. Thanks.

Tl;dr: I know what to do now. Finishing the schematic next time.
